PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the Award dated 11.09.2012 passed in M.V.C.No.324/2010 by the VII Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes MACT (SCCH-3) whereby the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.1,96,415/-.
2.

entities.text: VII Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes MACT (SCCH-3)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.14,00,000/- and the Tribunal had granted an amount of Rs.1,96,415/-.

It is the case of the claimant that on 11.10.2009, he was proceeding as a paid passenger in a car from Kanakapura to Bangalore and the driver of the car drove in a rash and negligent manner and collided with a bus.
As a result, the claimant sustained injuries and was shifted to a local hospital and then shifted to Nimhans Hospital, Bangalore.
The claimant had spent an amount of Rs.80,000/- for treatment NC: 2023:KHC:33084 and conveyance charges.
The injuries resulted in permanent disability.

The Court below, on the issue of negligence,
had held that the accident had taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.

When it comes to the compensation, as it is the case of the claimant that he was working as a tailor and earning an amount of Rs.12,000/- per month and as there was no evidence in that regard,
the Court below had considered an amount of Rs.5,000/- as income
. It is the case of the claimant that he had sustained disability because of the injuries.

The Court below considering the injuries and the evidence of the doctor who has stated that claimant suffered 35% of permanent disability to his right leg and 16% to the whole body, taking 16% as disability and applying the multiplier of 15,
granted an amount of Rs.1,44,000/- under the head of loss of income due to disability.

Towards pain and agony, an amount of Rs.20,000/-, towards actual medical bills, an amount of Rs.1,914/-,
towards attendant charges for one month an amount of Rs.4,500/-, towards food and nutrition an amount of Rs.6,000/-, towards loss of income during the laid up period considering an amount of Rs.5,000/- as income granted for one month Rs.5,000/- and for loss of amenities an amount of Rs.15,000/- was granted.
NC: 2023:KHC:33084 Altogether, compensation of an amount of Rs.1,96,415/- was granted.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that she had to be in hospital for a long time and as the injury is fracture of leg, the Court granted compensation of an amount of Rs.5,000/-
under the head of loss of income during the laid up period which is not reasonable.
Further, towards attendant charges, food and nourishment, only an amount of Rs.10,500/- was granted.
Learned counsel submits that even under the other heads also the amounts that were granted were not reasonable.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that considering the evidence and all the relevant aspects, the Court below had rightly granted the compensation.
It is submitted that no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the entire material on record.
According to the claimant, he was working as a tailor and earning an amount of Rs.12,000/-.
There is no evidence that he was earning an amount of Rs.12,000/- per month.
The Court had taken an amount of Rs.5,000/- as income.

In the case of an agricultural NC: 2023:KHC:33084 labour,
without there being any evidence, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ramachandrappa V/s Manager Royal Sundaram Alliance1 had taken an amount of Rs.4,500/- whereas in the case of skill works like mechanic, electrician, driver, the Hon'ble Apex Court had taken an amount of Rs.6,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa V/s Manager Royal Sundaram Alliance1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the claimant is a tailor.
His work is a skilled work.

Hence, considering these facts, this Court deems it appropriate to take an amount of Rs.6,000/- as the income and considering 16% as the disability, loss of income due to disability would come to 6,000x12x15x16%
i.e., Rs.1,72,800/-.
Considering the injuries suffered and the prolonged hospitalization, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.

Towards medical bills and loss of amenities, the Court below had rightly granted an amount of Rs.1,914/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively and no interference is called for, under these heads towards the attendant charges, extra nourishment and transport,

Court below had granted an amount of Rs.10,500/- and this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.15,000/- for the prolonged hospitalization, for the loss of income during the laid up period, 2011 (13) SCC 236 NC: 2023:KHC:33084 the Court below had granted the amount only for one month.
The injuries are to the legs and he is a tailor.

In those circumstances, under the head of loss of income he is entitled for a period of four months,
considering the income at Rs.6,000/-, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.24,000/-.

6. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER2, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.

7. The claimant is therefore, entitled to the compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Compensation  Awarded

1. Loss of income due to disability : Rs. 1,72,800/-
2. Pain and suffering : Rs. 30,000/-
3.

Medical Bills : Rs. 1,914/-

ii. The enhanced amount shall carry 6% interest p.a.
